summary: Hardened /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) with noexec,nosuid,nodev, made it reboot-persistent, and verified both the mount options and functional enforcement (exec denied, device nodes denied) before and after a full node restart with a changed boot ID.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: /tmp was part of root ext4 fs (no separate mount); /dev/shm was tmpfs with only nosuid,nodev
Backed up /etc/fstab, added a bind-mount fstab entry for /tmp (bind,noexec,nosuid,nodev) and a tmpfs fstab entry for /dev/shm (defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev)

Discovered bind mounts on this system don't apply extra options via a single mount -a pass, so created /etc/systemd/system/tmp-hardening.service (oneshot, After=tmp.mount, Before=local-fs.target, WantedBy=local-fs.target) to remount /tmp with the hardened options at every boot, and enabled it
Applied changes live and verified via findmnt that both /tmp and /dev/shm show rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec

Functionally verified enforcement pre-restart: script execution from /tmp and /dev/shm returned exit 126 (Permission denied), and reading a root-owned mknod'd character device in either mount returned Permission denied
Captured baseline boot_id (1f0657c2-...) and mount state
Triggered a native single-node reboot (systemctl reboot via backgrounded sudo sh -c 'sleep 2; systemctl reboot') so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed to 4b123f3b-... proving an actual restart occurred

Re-verified post-restart: findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm still carry noexec,nosuid,nodev; tmp-hardening.service is enabled and active; re-ran the exec and device-node functional tests, both blocked identically to pre-restart
Cleaned up all test artifacts (exectest.sh, testdev nodes) on both mounts

evidence.requirement: Baseline mount/config state before any changes
evidence.summary: Showed /tmp had no separate mount and /dev/shm lacked noexec before hardening

evidence.requirement: fstab updated with hardened options for /tmp and /dev/shm
evidence.summary: Backed up fstab then appended bind/tmpfs entries with noexec,nosuid,nodev

evidence.requirement: Discovery that bind mount needs an explicit remount step, and creation of persistent systemd remount unit
evidence.summary: Proved mount -a alone doesn't apply bind options; added and enabled tmp-hardening.service which correctly remounts /tmp with the required flags

evidence.requirement: Live functional proof that exec, setuid, and device nodes are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Script execution returned exit 126 on both mounts; device node read returned Permission denied on both mounts (nosuid covered by findmnt option confirmation since noexec already blocks all execution including setuid binaries)

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + mount state) for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 1f0657c2-c163-4ef6-be0b-3118b10aa595 plus findmnt output confirming hardened options and enabled/active service, prior to restart
Backgrounded sudo reboot command with a 2s delay; exec call returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED successfully before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id was unchanged, then connection was refused during reboot, then boot_id returned as 4b123f3b-ec2e-4211-8c68-982213933b4d, a different value confirming an actual restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: hardened mount options persisted and service is healthy
evidence.summary: findmnt confirms both /tmp and /dev/shm retain nosuid,nodev,noexec after reboot; tmp-hardening.service is enabled and active (exited 0) post-boot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional proof that exec/device restrictions are enforced
evidence.summary: After reboot, script execution on /tmp and /dev/shm again returned exit 126, and device-node reads again returned Permission denied on both mounts
